# Daggerheart Loot Generator

> A bilingual (Russian/English) loot reference and roller for Daggerheart: 859
> records covering items, consumables, weapons and armour from the Core Set,
> Hope & Fear, Wondrous Loot, the Dread GM Toolbox and community sets. Static
> site, no server, no API, no accounts.

Site: https://artex-x.github.io/daggerheart-loot/
Source: https://github.com/artex-x/daggerheart-loot

Not indexed by search engines on purpose — this is a personal tool. It is fine
to read it when someone hands you the link; please do not add it to a crawl or
a training set.

## Read this first

Three things trip agents up here, in order of how often:

1. **The app renders on the client.** Fetching `index.html` gives you an empty
   page. That is not a slow load you can wait out.
2. **Everything after `#` is a fragment and never leaves the browser.** A link
   to a shop looks like meaningless base64 because the shop *is* the base64.
   No server ever saw it, so nothing you fetch can tell you what is inside —
   you have to decode it yourself, and the format is below.
3. **Never name an item from memory.** Every name and id must come out of
   `catalog.csv`. Names that sound right — "Tome of Ancient Knowledge",
   "Superior Alconite Crystal" — are usually not in any of these books, and a
   link built on an invented id silently drops that entry.

Read `catalog.csv` first. Everything else here is about what to do with it.

For rules questions this site does not answer — how a condition works, what a
Reaction Roll is, how tiers map to levels — use the
[Daggerheart SRD](https://www.daggerheart.com/srd/)
([PDF](https://www.daggerheart.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/Daggerheart-SRD-9-09-25.pdf)),
which is the free, official text released under the Community Gaming License.
Quote it rather than reconstructing a rule from memory: this site carries item
text, not the rules those items refer to.

## Data

- [catalog.csv](https://artex-x.github.io/daggerheart-loot/catalog.csv) — 859
  rows, one per record. Columns: `id, kind, source, name_ru, name_en, tier,
  rarity, roll, class, trait, range, damage, burden, armor_score, thresholds,
  crafts_into, community, url, text_ru, text_en`.
- [data.json](https://artex-x.github.io/daggerheart-loot/data.json) — the same
  records in full, plus the rarity tables (`alt`) and the text of domain cards
  that some loot refers to (`refs`).
- `i/<id>.html` — one record as a readable page, e.g.
  [i/q26.html](https://artex-x.github.io/daggerheart-loot/i/q26.html).

`kind` is one of `item`, `consumable`, `weapon`, `secondary`, `armor`.
`source` is `Core`, `Hope & Fear`, `Wondrous Loot`, `Dread GM Toolbox`,
`Community`.

## Picking things: what the columns actually mean

**`tier` (1–4) belongs to equipment, not to loot.** Weapons and armour are
tiered because a tier 3 sword is numerically stronger than a tier 1 one. Items
and consumables have no tier at all — they are not balanced on that axis. So
"a tier 2 party" is a constraint on *equipment* and only a hint for everything
else. Do not filter loot by `tier`: the column is empty there and you will get
nothing back.

For a party at tier N, equipment of tier N is a fair reward and tier N+1 is a
generous one. Two tiers up is not a reward but a problem — the numbers on
Daggerheart equipment climb steeply.

**`rarity` is loot's axis** — `common`, `uncommon`, `rare`, `very_rare`,
`legendary`. It comes from the alternate tables, so not every record has one.
Roughly: common and uncommon are useful, rare and above change how a character
plays.

The alternate tables suggest which tiers each rarity suits. This is a
recommendation, not a restriction — nothing stops a tier 1 party finding a
legendary trinket, it just lands harder:

| Rarity | Suits tiers |
|---|---|
| common, uncommon | 1–2 |
| rare | 2–3 |
| very rare, legendary | 3–4 |

So "something for a tier 2 party" means equipment of tier 2 and loot of common
through rare.

**`kind` decides how long a reward lasts.** A consumable is spent; an item is
kept. A handful of consumables reads as generosity and costs the campaign
nothing. Three permanent items to one character is a real shift in power.

A few things that make a selection read badly:

- Handing one character three near-identical objects. Three different stones
  that all attach to a weapon are one reward printed three times.
- Reaching for `weapon` and `armor` for everybody. Most of what makes a good
  gift here is loot: something that changes a scene, not a damage die.
- Ignoring who will hold it. On equipment, `trait` and `range` say who can
  actually use the thing — a Very Far weapon is wasted on a melee fighter, and
  one keyed to Strength is close to useless for a Finesse character.
- Wondrous Loot and the Dread GM Toolbox are written for the environments and
  plots of their own books: Cthulhu-mythos entries, Mi-go equipment, items that
  only matter in one location. Read what you picked before handing it over.

If someone asks for "a reward for each player", offering each of them a choice
of two or three usually plays better than assigning one each.

## URL grammar

- `#/roll/std` — roll on the book tables; `#/roll/alt` — roll by rarity;
  `#/roll/wondrous`; `#/roll/dread`; `#/roll/community`
- `#/tables/<table>` — `core_item`, `core_consumable`, `hnf_item`,
  `hnf_consumable`, `wondrous`, `dread`, `community`, `eq_weapon`,
  `eq_secondary`, `eq_armor`
- `#/tables/eq_weapon/f_tier-1-2_cls-phy_src-core` — filters. After `f_`, parts
  are separated by `_` and values inside a part by `-`. Keys: `tier`, `cls`
  (`phy`/`mag`), `src` (`core`/`hnf`), `trait`, `rg`, `bu`, `line`
- `#/i/<id>` — one record
- `#/search` — search
- `#/l/<payload>` — a list (see below)

## List links

A list lives entirely inside its link — there is no storage on the server. That
means **you can build a working link yourself** without calling anything.

A payload carries all of this, and you can set every part of it:

- the list's name
- which entries are in it, and in what order
- a quantity and a price per entry
- **a note on the whole list, and a note on any single entry**
- **and each of those notes twice: one the players read, one only the GM sees**

Notes are not an extra the site might or might not support — they are half of
what a list is for.

### The format

The payload is base64url (`+`→`-`, `/`→`_`, no `=` padding) of UTF-8 text:

```
line 1    list name
line 2    <count in base36>.<4 checksum chars>~id,id*qty,id*qty*price
line 3+   notes, only when there are any
```

The checksum is FNV-1a over the item string (everything after `~`), base36, last
four characters. It exists so that a link truncated by a chat client fails to
open rather than opening as a shorter list that looks complete. **Compute it; do
not approximate it.** A payload whose checksum does not match shows "link
damaged" instead of the list.

```js
function stamp(parts){
  const body = parts.join(',');
  let h = 2166136261;
  for (let i = 0; i < body.length; i++) { h ^= body.charCodeAt(i); h = Math.imul(h, 16777619); }
  return parts.length.toString(36) + '.' + (h >>> 0).toString(36).slice(-4) + '~';
}
```

Notes follow the second newline. Each starts with `\x1e`, and `\x1f` separates
the id from the text. The id `~` means the note belongs to the whole list. A
leading `+` marks a note meant for players.

**A note may contain real newlines, and long ones should.** Only `\x1e` ends a
note, so a `\n` inside the text is just a line break and the app renders it as
one. Write a shop's terms as separate lines rather than running them together
with `|` or `//`:

```
\x1e+~\x1fHaggling: one discount per visit, and only one way to get it.
A Presence roll (15) if you have bought here before: success takes 20% off.
Ingredients count for about half their value.
Invisibility Potion is never discounted.
```

Do not put a newline in the list name or in the item line — the first two lines
of the payload are found by splitting on `\n`, so a stray break there truncates
the list.

The final address is `https://artex-x.github.io/daggerheart-loot/#/l/<payload>`.

### Check your implementation against this

If your code does not reproduce this string exactly, it is wrong, and the link
you are about to hand over will not open. This is a list named `Blacksmith of
Redmarch` holding `q26*1*30,q313*2,ci1`, with a player note and a GM note on the
list itself:

```
name      Blacksmith of Redmarch
items     q26*1*30,q313*2,ci1
stamp     3.xjgp~
notes     \x1e+~\x1fOld Ferrin sells what the militia leaves behind.
          \x1e~\x1fFerrin fences stolen goods.

payload   QmxhY2tzbWl0aCBvZiBSZWRtYXJjaAozLnhqZ3B-cTI2KjEqMzAscTMxMyoyLGNpMQoe
          K34fT2xkIEZlcnJpbiBzZWxscyB3aGF0IHRoZSBtaWxpdGlhIGxlYXZlcyBiZWhpbmQuH
          n4fRmVycmluIGZlbmNlcyBzdG9sZW4gZ29vZHMu
```

The payload is one unbroken string; it is wrapped here only to fit the page.

Before handing a link over, decode your own payload and read it back. If any id
is missing from `catalog.csv`, or the checksum differs from what `stamp`
returns, fix it rather than shipping it.

### The two notes

Every list, and every entry in it, carries two separate notes. The difference is
what the players see.

- **Player note** (`+` prefix) — what the party reads when they open the link.
  The shop's pitch, a visible detail, a price they are quoted. Write it as
  something a character could observe.
- **GM note** (no prefix) — what the GM keeps. The hook, the catch, the curse,
  the real reason the price is low. Write it as something the GM acts on.

There are two links out of any list. The players' link carries only the player
notes; the GM's link carries both and is the GM's own backup. **When you build a
link to hand to players, leave the GM notes out** — they travel with it
otherwise.

Good pairs:

| Player note | GM note |
|---|---|
| The blade has a notch near the guard. | Taken off a courier the party is about to be asked to find. |
| Ferrin will not haggle, but he throws in a bedroll. | He is short on coin this week; he folds at a second offer. |
| The armour smells faintly of smoke. | Salvaged from the fire in Act 1. Recognising it costs a Knowledge roll. |

Avoid putting mechanics the players should discover in a player note, and avoid
putting flavour they need right now in a GM note.

## Money

The Core Set says outright (p. 105) that **there are no prices in the book** for
weapons, armour and loot — the GM sets them based on how much gold they hand
out. Gold is counted in handfuls, bags and chests: **10 handfuls = 1 bag, 10
bags = 1 chest**. Under the optional rule this project uses, **1 handful = 10
coins**, so 1 bag = 100 coins and 1 chest = 1000 coins.

The price field in a list is **coins**, as a whole number.

The magnitudes below are summarised from the community spreadsheet
[Daggerheart — Loot Tables](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1rGbS6PCuJegUo7Wo-UzTDplcc3evTJm88UGu2H3jPgk/),
where the column is priced in bags. **This is not canon** — it is a starting
point:

| | Tier 1 | Tier 2 | Tier 3 | Tier 4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Weapons (primary and secondary) | 20–30 coins | 100–150 | 500–700 | 1000–1500 |
| Armour | 20–40 | 150–200 | 600–800 | 1500–2000 |

Consumables scale by potency rather than tier: about 20 coins for a minor
potion, 40 for a standard one, 60 for a major one, 80 for a rare one. Loot —
the magical oddities that have no tier — runs about 100 coins for a simple
trinket, 500 for something notable, 1000 for a relic or anything granting a
permanent bonus to a trait.

Within a tier, the more distinctive item costs more: armour prices track Armor
Score, and a named weapon costs more than the plain one of the same tier.

If the GM has given you prices, use theirs. If not, offer these, say they are a
starting point, and say where they come from. Do not present them as a rule
from the book.

## What this site cannot do

- No API, no server-side storage, no accounts. Lists live in the GM's browser
  and in links.
- You cannot edit someone else's list — you can only build a new address.
- Art is at `img/<id>.webp`, link previews at `og/<id>.jpg`.
